verdict.root_cause: frontend's CART_ADDR environment variable was re-applied by platform-automation at 08:24:32 pointing at cart:7071, a port nothing is listening on. frontend restarted a second later [tr_ffd09da66365], picked up the wrong endpoint, and every outbound gRPC call to CartService began failing immediately with status 14 UNAVAILABLE / connection refused against the resolved address 172.18.0.24:7071. The wrongness of the value is the failure: cart itself is healthy and serving, so only the frontend code paths that dial the misconfigured endpoint (/api/cart GetCart and AddItem) break, and the errors propagate outward to frontend-proxy, checkout and the load generator, which is why those services alerted after frontend.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge. (1) The only change on frontend in the window is the same key, CART_ADDR, set to cart:7071 about three minutes before onset by platform-automation, and the identical value had been applied and backed out hours earlier — a re-application of a previously reverted change [tr_8b2c437c958a]. (2) frontend's own log shows a clean start at 08:24:33 with no internal fault, followed immediately and continuously by a single error class: gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE, connection refused, against one address and port, 172.18.0.24:7071 [tr_ffd09da66365]. A refusal at TCP connect on a resolved IP excludes DNS, TLS/auth, overload and timeout. (3) Traces show error spans terminating only at frontend's CartService client calls, with no cart server-side span and sub-millisecond-to-2ms durations — immediate rejection, not slowness — while every non-cart route in the same window succeeds [tr_36d896dacae9]. The culprit side is exonerated: cart's error ratio is flat zero with no sample gaps across 08:24-08:28 [tr_170c77c4641d], its logs show uninterrupted cart-store work right up to 08:29:29 with no restart or binding event and no refusals [tr_81299862b448], and its only changes were image-tag churn ending 2.6h before onset, leaving it on the reverted reference with no port or service-spec edit anywhere [tr_2a12a40350e5]. So cart is up and answering someone — just not on 7071. The frontend error-ratio change point at 08:27:46 with a window max ~3.5x the baseline max anchors onset and confirms this is a late, sharp excursion rather than a slow burn [tr_caa1c51c6bda]. The mechanism is the wrong value in the config, not exhaustion, not waiting, not a bad artifact (no deploy or image event exists for frontend), so the fix is to revert CART_ADDR to the endpoint cart actually serves and prevent automation from re-applying it.
open_questions: Cart's actual listening port was never directly observed — its logs contain no bind or listener lines [tr_81299862b448] and no deployment/service spec was pulled. The 7071-is-wrong conclusion is inferred from the refusal on the frontend side plus cart's continued healthy service to other callers, not confirmed from cart's config.
Why platform-automation re-applied a value that had already been reverted twice is unexplained; without that, a revert may simply be re-applied again.

Both log results were truncated (frontend 8 oldest / 32 newest, cart roughly 07:57-08:28 unobserved), so the interval between the 08:24:33 restart and the 08:27:46 change point is not directly characterised on either side.

No frontend latency percentiles, CPU, memory or connection-pool data were returned [tr_caa1c51c6bda], so a concurrent resource issue on frontend is unmeasured, though nothing in logs or traces suggests one.

The gap between the 08:24:33 restart with immediate errors and the 08:27:46 metric change point (~3 minutes) is not fully explained — likely rate-window smoothing or cached channel state [tr_ffd09da66365], but not demonstrated.
checkout also calls cart; whether checkout uses a separate, correct endpoint (which would explain cart's continued zero-error traffic) was not investigated — no dispatch touched checkout.

alternatives.root_cause: cart's listener genuinely moved off 7071 (or never bound it) due to something outside the recorded change log, making frontend's config correct and cart the faulty party.
alternatives.why_not: cart's change history contains no port, service-spec or containerPort edit at all — only image-tag churn ending 2.6h before onset [tr_2a12a40350e5] — and cart keeps serving successful calls with a flat-zero error ratio and unbroken sample coverage through the onset minutes [tr_170c77c4641d, tr_81299862b448]. A listener that moved would have disrupted its other callers too. The only thing that demonstrably changed minutes before onset is frontend's CART_ADDR [tr_8b2c437c958a]. It stays on the list only because cart's bind address was never directly read.

alternatives.root_cause: frontend was restarted at 08:24:33 into a state where its cart gRPC channel is permanently wedged, and a restart rather than a config change is what is needed.
alternatives.why_not: frontend starts cleanly and reports ready in ~209ms with no internal exception, crash loop or build failure, and its change log contains no deploy, release or image event — only environment edits [tr_ffd09da66365, tr_8b2c437c958a]. The running artifact is the right one; it is simply pointed at a port nothing answers on. A restart would re-read the same wrong CART_ADDR and reproduce the refusals.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring frontend's prior environment (CART_ADDR absent, as it stood after the 04:43:01 revert) and recreating the container should stop the repeating gRPC status 14 UNAVAILABLE / connection refused lines against 172.18.0.24:7071 in {service="frontend"} logs — the last such line should be within seconds of the recreate. Frontend's error-ratio series (sum rate STATUS_CODE_ERROR / sum rate calls, 5m window) should fall from its ~0.19-0.27 excursion back under the ~0.12 detection threshold and toward the baseline mean of ~0.029 within roughly two rate-windows. In traces, /api/cart GetCart and AddItem client spans should regain matching cart server-side spans and lose their error status; frontend-proxy, checkout and load-generator error ratios should follow frontend down, since trace evidence shows their errors are inherited from frontend's cart branch. Cart's own error ratio should stay flat at zero throughout — it never moved.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, more than ~60s after the recreate, frontend still logs connection-refused to a cart endpoint: (a) still to :7071 — the revert did not take, or platform-automation re-applied the value a third time (unexplained in this investigation, and the single largest reason this fix may not hold); (b) to a different address/port — then the pre-change default is also wrong and cart's real listening port must be read from its deployment/service spec, which was never pulled; cart's own logs cannot settle it [tr_81299862b448]. Also falsified if frontend's error ratio stays above ~0.12 after two 5m rate windows while cart client spans now succeed — that would mean a second, unmeasured failure mode on frontend (no latency, CPU, memory or connection-pool data was returned [tr_caa1c51c6bda]). A weaker warning sign: frontend fails to reach Ready after recreate, meaning the prior config is incomplete rather than merely different.
proposal.risk: If CART_ADDR=cart:7071 was in fact correct and the refusal has another cause (cart bound elsewhere, a network-level block), this removes the only explicit cart endpoint from frontend and leaves it on a compiled-in default that may be equally wrong or absent — frontend could fail to start or break cart paths in a new way, and we would have spent a restart without learning anything. Cart's actual listening port was never directly observed, so the premise that 7071 is wrong is inferred, not confirmed. The recreate itself discards frontend's in-process cache and resets its gRPC channels, which is cheap here but not free. There is also a real chance platform-automation re-applies the bad value minutes later, producing a second identical outage; this action does not address the automation loop, which is outside what this system may do and needs a human to stop the actor.
proposal.blast_radius: One service is changed, frontend, but its callers feel the recreate: frontend-proxy, and through it load-generator, will see connections reset and a brief burst of 5xx/connection errors for the few seconds frontend is down (it reported Ready in ~209ms previously, so expect a short interruption). checkout calls frontend's upstream path and may see the same blip. cart is the service the reverted value points at: it should begin receiving GetCart/AddItem traffic from frontend again, raising its request rate from its current frontend-free level — it was already serving other callers at zero errors, so this is added load, not new risk. ad, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation, currency, email, payment and shipping are untouched except for the same momentary gap in any in-flight frontend request.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service failure spanning frontend, proxy, and checkout with user-visible impact; nothing here can be dismissed. Fault class is not implied by the alert pattern alone, so downstream dependency checks of checkout/frontend should decide it.
